The dates between now and late January that matter
Four things to do with this stretch
intro: If you are a Cancer by Moon sign, the next two months are less about what happens to you and more about what you believe. Old rules, the ones you picked up from family, school or a teacher you looked up to, are being tested. Some of them still fit. Some of them quietly don't, and it can feel like standing between an old way of living and a new one.

That is uncomfortable, but it is not a bad sign. The tradition reads this kind of stretch as the time your beliefs become your own. Two dates change the mood: December 5, when a calm, inward influence arrives on your sign, and December 10, when slow, stuck questions start moving again. Through it all, home and family stay warm.

sections.label: Beliefs
title: Outgrowing
old rules.
paragraphs: The slowest, most serious influence in the sky sits in your house of beliefs, teachers, long journeys and luck. It is read as a period of questioning: the things you were taught about work, love, money or faith get examined one by one, and some of them don't survive the look.

It can feel like being stuck between two lives, with the old way pulling you back and the new one not quite ready. The tradition's upside is clear. What you still believe at the end of this is said to be truly yours, chosen instead of inherited, and that kind of belief holds up for years.
It has been moving backwards, which tends to bring the same questions round again and again. On December 10 it turns forward. The questions don't vanish, but answers start to arrive.

sections.label: Your inner life
title: A quiet,
inward stretch.
paragraphs: On December 5 a calm, detached influence, the tail of the eclipse axis, lands on your own sign, and it stays well beyond these two months. It is read as a quieter, more inward time: less interest in noise, crowds and proving yourself, and more interest in what is really going on inside.

Some people with this placement feel a little hard to read, even to themselves. That is normal. Rest, time alone, journaling and anything spiritual or reflective tend to go well, and it is a good stretch to let go of an old image of yourself that no longer fits.

sections.label: Home and money
title: Where the
warmth is.
paragraphs: The planet of luck and growth is in your house of family, money and speech until January 23. It is read as a warm stretch for home: meals together, kinder words, a fuller table. Your voice carries weight too, so this is a good time to say what you need from the people closest to you.

From December 12 that influence slows and appears to move backwards for a while, which is read as a time to review, not to start: look at the family budget, settle an old conversation. On January 24 it moves onto your own sign, a big change that the tradition reads as growth, and the start of a new chapter.

sections.label: Partners
title: New people
come close.
paragraphs: Until December 4 a restless, hungry influence sits in your house of deep change, read as sudden shifts and a fascination with hidden things. On December 5 it moves into your house of partners, and stays there well beyond these two months.

There it is read as new, unusual people coming close: a partner, a business contact or a friend from a very different world. It can be exciting. The usual advice is to enjoy the newness and take your time before you promise anything.

steps.name: Write down your rules
steps.text: List five things you were taught about how life should go. Next to each, write whether it still feels true. Keep the ones that do.

steps.name: Let the rest go gently
steps.text: No dramatic breaks. Just stop acting on the rules that no longer fit, one at a time, and notice how it feels.

steps.name: Protect your quiet
steps.text: From December 5 your energy turns inward. Leave gaps in the calendar and don't apologise for needing them.

steps.name: Gather your people at home
steps.text: Home is the warmest part of your life until late January. Host the dinner, make the call, say the kind thing.

faq.q: Is this for my Sun sign or my Moon sign?
faq.a: Your Moon sign. Vedic astrology reads timing from the sign the Moon was in when you were born, which is often different from the Sun sign most people know.

faq.q: I’m a Cancer Sun. Does this apply to me?
faq.a: Only if your Moon is also in Cancer. Many people with a Cancer Sun have their Moon somewhere else. Your birth chart shows it in a few seconds.

faq.q: Is it bad to have this influence on my sign?
faq.a: No. In the tradition it is read as detachment, not loss: a time to look inward and drop what no longer fits. Many people find it a calm and clarifying stretch.

note: Dates are US Eastern time. Vedic (sidereal) astrology, read by Moon sign.
